name: ReSlot — Ghost Replay (3D picking-floor twin you can beat)
one_liner: A fully static, in-browser 3D warehouse twin driven by one real month of UCI Online Retail II orders: a picker replays every invoice along aisle-constrained exact (Held–Karp) routes; the player re-slots products and races a semi-transparent "ghost" picker walking the old layout on the same orders, scored on a held-out half of the month against a fast-movers baseline and a simulated-annealing optimiser.
why_it_wins: (1) It is the only one of the 12 problems where the must-have IS the spectacle: every hour on the 3D scene is an hour on requirement M2, so the demo is polished without starving the MVP. (2) Measured, not claimed: the ghost-vs-solid replay race shows two counters diverging live on identical orders, then the KPI card reports held-out numbers (second half of November 2011) that the player never optimised on; judges who ask "show me the split" get it on screen. (3) Zero-failure demo by construction: pure static Vite build on Vercel with a Cloudflare Pages mirror, no backend, no LLM key, no rate limits, no cold start, no map tiles, no HDR/asset CDN fetch, deterministic simulation (same orders + same layout = identical metres every click), runs offline from `vite preview` if venue Wi-Fi dies. (4) Technical depth that survives expert Q&A: aisle-graph all-pairs shortest paths, exact Held–Karp DP tour per order (<=12 stops) with NN+2-opt/Or-opt above, Hall-1993 S-shape/return heuristics as a live routing ablation, and a simulated-annealing slotting optimiser with incremental delta evaluation that captures order affinity (co-picked SKUs end up in the same aisle), which the required ABC baseline cannot; in-sample vs held-out gain of the optimiser is reported side by side. (5) Low pick rate: three.js intimidates ML-first teams, so the field is thin, and judge-mindset ranks 4.2 as highest reward. Why not the alternatives from my demo-safety lens: 4.3 needs a Python solver backend (HF free Docker Spaces now need PRO per tonight's docs check; Render free cold-starts ~60 s) or a weaker browser-only solver, plus venue-Wi-Fi map tiles; 3.3's wow (3D highlight) is a stretch goal, so visual hours do not count toward must-haves; 2.3 needs training compute and shows grayscale 200x200 crops. 4.2 makes every risk an engineering risk we control, and every number on screen is computed live from real order lines.
demo_script:
Pre-flight (10 min before slot): live URL open in tab 1, local `npm run preview` in tab 2, MP4 on desktop, laptop on power, browser 110% zoom, "Quality: auto" verified at 60 fps, hash-link of the rehearsed player layout ready in clipboard.

0:00–0:20 Slide 1–2 (narrator): "Pickers walk more than they pick. Where a product sits decides how far." One-liner, PS 4.2, QR codes for live app + repo.

0:20–0:45 Switch to live app (already loaded). Scripted intro camera flight (drei CameraControls.setLookAt tween): dock -> down aisle 3 at picker height -> rise to 3/4 isometric. Racks are coloured by real pick frequency (InstancedMesh instanceColor heat ramp). Click the hottest box: tooltip "85123A WHITE HANGING HEART T-LIGHT HOLDER · 1,2xx picks in Nov 2011". Open Data panel: raw lines -> after removing C-invoices -> after removing non-product codes -> top-100 coverage X% -> N orders, split opt (1–15 Nov) / held-out (16–30 Nov). WOW 1: the data-driven heat racks + provenance in 10 seconds.

0:45–1:40 M2 Replay. Press Play. HUD shows "Invoice 581587 · 7 lines". Cyan path draws itself ahead of the picker along the aisle centre lines (drei Line with growing points, Bloom), the picker walks at 20x, picked boxes pulse, distance and time counters tick (motion animate). Operator toggles "Route: optimal (DP) -> S-shape" on the same order: path re-draws, metres change; narrator: "walking follows aisles, never through racks; the DP tour is exact under the aisle metric". Press "Simulate whole month": worker scores all orders in <1 s, total km appears. Press it again: identical number (determinism, said out loud).

1:40–2:40 M3 Game. Press "Baseline: fast movers nearest dock": 100 boxes fly to new slots (instance matrix lerp), KPI card: Original -> Baseline on opt and held-out sets. Now the player: drag JUMBO BAG RED RETROSPOT next to WHITE HANGING HEART (co-picked pair, shown by the affinity hint); narrator explains affinity. Press "Replay Race": WOW 2: amber ghost picker (old layout, 35% opacity) and solid picker (new layout) walk the SAME invoice simultaneously; two counters diverge live; floor tiles under both paths accumulate heat. After ~8 orders, stop; KPI card updates: Player vs Baseline vs Original on held-out orders.

2:40–3:30 AI opponent. Press "Run optimiser (8 s)": SA runs in the Web Worker, live objective curve drops, temperature readout; result layout applied with box-fly animation. KPI: SA beats baseline by Y% in-sample and Z% held-out; narrator says the held-out number is the one that counts and that it is smaller. Leaderboard shows Player, SA, Baseline, Original. Share-link button copies a URL hash with the layout; a judge can open it on their phone (2D slot map mode).

3:30–4:10 Evidence panel (in-app, same code as `npm run eval`): table of total distance and avg pick time per order for Original / Baseline / SA / Player on opt and held-out; routing ablation (optimal vs S-shape vs nearest-neighbour); coverage %; count of orders routed heuristically (>12 stops) flagged. Show README screenshot with identical numbers and the commit hash they were generated at.

4:10–4:40 Stretch demonstrated only if done and measured: two pickers with aisle congestion (second picker waits at aisle entrance; time delta shown) or batch picking cart (3 orders/trip, metres saved). Then limitations, spoken: layout is ours, "original" layout is a declared StockCode-order convention, constant 8 s handling per line, single-level racks, UK gift retailer data from 2011, top-100 SKUs cover only X% of lines.

4:40–5:00 Team, module ownership, AI tools declared (Claude Code agents; human line-by-line review), #NEXAI2026 links. Q&A cards ready: split, original layout, why DP is exact, SA delta evaluation, coverage, what breaks, performance budget, what is synthetic.
wow_visual: 1) HEAT RACKS: one `InstancedMesh` of 100 SKU boxes (plus 12 empty slots) with `instanceColor` from pick frequency (perceptual ramp sampled in JS from blue #1e3a8a -> cyan -> amber -> #f97316); rack uprights/shelves as drei `<Instances>` (two draw calls total); floor tiles as one InstancedMesh (8 aisles x 7 bays + 2 cross-aisles ~ 130 tiles) whose instanceColor accumulates visits during replay ("heat memory"). 2) SELF-DRAWING PATH + TICKING COUNTERS: route polyline from the sim's node list rendered with drei `<Line>` (Line2, lineWidth 3, cyan #22d3ee) whose `points` slice grows ahead of the picker; `motion@14.5.0` `animate(from,to,{onUpdate})` for metre/second counters; picked box gets a 300 ms emissive pulse. 3) GHOST REPLAY RACE: the picker is a procedural low-poly rig (capsule body, sphere head, box cart with 4 cylinder wheels; no GLTF/asset fetch); the ghost reuses the same component with `MeshBasicMaterial transparent opacity 0.35 depthWrite=false`, amber path, walking the previous layout's route for the same invoice at the same speed; both counters diverge live. 4) BOX-FLY RELAYOUT: on baseline/SA/player apply, each instance lerps from old slot to new slot over 0.8 s with ease-out (instanceMatrix needsUpdate per frame), so the change in layout is visible as motion. 5) CAMERA CHOREOGRAPHY: drei `<CameraControls>` (camera-controls 3.1.2) with `setLookAt(...,true)` presets (Dock, Isometric, Follow-picker with smoothTime 0.4) and a scripted intro flight. 6) POST-FX WITH QUALITY GUARD: `@react-three/postprocessing@3.2.1` + `postprocessing@6.39.5` Bloom (luminanceThreshold 0.6, mipmapBlur) and SMAA; auto-tier from a 2-second FPS probe at load; "low" tier disables post-FX, caps dpr to 1, and keeps draw calls < 50; `frameloop="demand"` when idle, "always" during replay. 7) 2D SLOT MAP side panel (plain React SVG, same colours) mirrored with the 3D, with click-to-select/click-to-swap, current order path polyline, and affinity hints (top co-picked SKUs of the selected product); this is also the phone/2D fallback. Theme: dark slate #0b1020 background, steel racks, hemisphere + one directional light, no shadows, no environment maps; projector-safe HUD fonts >= 18 px, numerals monospace. All data (JSON < 1 MB) bundled; first load ~2 MB gzipped.
wow_technical: Core: a headless, deterministic simulator `simulate(layout, orders, routingPolicy)` shared by scoring, animation and the eval script. (a) Aisle graph: 8 aisles x 2 sides x 7 bays = 112 slots; nodes = dock (front-left corner), per-aisle front/back ends, one node per bay position on the aisle centre line (serves both sides); edges = bay pitch 1.2 m along aisles, 5.0 m between adjacent aisle ends on the 4 m cross-aisles (aisle width 3.0 m + 2 x 1.0 m rack depth); Dijkstra all-pairs on ~73 nodes -> Float32Array distance matrix; walking can only use these edges, so paths never cross racks. (b) Exact intra-order routing: stops deduplicated to nodes; Held–Karp DP over the metric closure for <= 12 stops (12^2 x 2^12 ~ 590k ops, ~1 ms) gives the provably optimal dock-to-dock tour under the aisle metric; > 12 stops uses nearest-neighbour + 2-opt + Or-opt and is flagged per order; Hall (1993) S-shape and return heuristics implemented as switchable policies for a live ablation. (c) Metrics: walking time = distance / 1.2 m/s, pick time = walking + 8 s x lines (both parameters in README and in-UI). (d) Required baseline: SKUs sorted by pick lines desc assigned to slots sorted by dock distance asc. (e) AI opponent: simulated annealing over slot permutations initialised from the baseline; objective = replayed total distance on the optimisation half; incremental delta evaluation via an SKU -> orders index (a swap re-routes only orders containing either SKU, cached per-order distances); T0 from the mean |delta| of 200 sampled swaps, geometric cooling to T0/1000, time-budgeted (8 s live, 60 s offline for the shipped `layouts/sa_seed42.json` with its log); move evaluation on a fixed 600-order subsample during search, full re-evaluation on acceptance milestones and at the end; this captures order affinity (co-occurrence), which ABC slotting ignores. (f) Honest evaluation: time-based split, orders 1–15 Nov 2011 = optimise set, 16–30 Nov = held-out; every layout (Original = StockCode-ascending row-major, Baseline, SA, Player) scored on both; routing-policy ablation on the same layout; coverage % of order lines represented by the top-100 SKUs; share of orders routed heuristically. (g) Tests (vitest): graph distances on a 2-aisle toy layout by hand, Held–Karp == brute force for n <= 7, SA delta == full recompute (property test over random swaps), `simulate` determinism, prep row counts asserted against meta. (h) `npm run eval` (tsx) regenerates `eval/results.md` with commit hash and timestamp, and a vitest "drift test" fails if the committed results.md differs from a fresh run, so README numbers cannot diverge from the app. Metrics that prove it: total walking distance (km) and average pick time per order for Original / Baseline / SA / Player on opt and held-out sets; SA in-sample vs held-out gain gap; optimal vs S-shape distance ratio.
mvp_mapping:
M1 (one month of order lines -> JSON: top ~100 products, pick frequency, order list): `prep/prep.py` reads the verified HF parquet mirror of Online Retail II (1,067,371 rows), filters InvoiceDate in [2011-11-01, 2011-12-01), drops Invoice starting with "C", Quantity <= 0, Price <= 0, null Description, exact duplicate rows (count reported), keeps StockCode matching `^\d{5}[A-Za-z]{0,2}$` and explicitly drops POST, D, M, S, DOT, BANK CHARGES, CRUK, ADJUST, AMAZONFEE, C2, PADS, TEST*, gift_*; ranks SKUs by number of invoices containing them (pick lines), takes top 100; emits `public/data/orders_2011-11.json` {meta:{source, licence, month, lines_raw, lines_after_cancel, lines_after_nonproduct, dedup_removed, lines_top100, coverage_pct, orders_opt, orders_test, generated_at, script_sha}, skus:[{code, desc, picks, units}], orders:[{id, ts, lines:[skuIdx...]}], split:{opt:[ids], test:[ids]}} (< 1 MB). Shown verbatim in the app's Data panel; click any box to see its StockCode and pick count.

M2 (3D grid warehouse with racks, aisles, packing dock, >= 1 animated picker, replaying orders along aisles with live distance and time counters): R3F scene with 8 aisles, 112 rack slots, front/back cross-aisles and a dock; the picker follows the exact node path produced by `sim/route.ts` over the aisle graph (never through racks), the current invoice ID and line count are on the HUD, distance and time counters tick per step; "Simulate whole month" scores every order headlessly in the Worker (< 1 s) so totals never depend on the animation; replay a subset at 20x with a speed slider.

M3 (game mode: swap/drag products between slots, replay the same orders, before/after walking distance and pick time, plus an automatic baseline of fast movers nearest the dock): drei `<DragControls>` with slot snapping in 3D plus click-to-swap in both 3D and the 2D slot map (fallback), moves into the 12 empty slots allowed; "Replay Race" replays the identical order list on old and new layouts (ghost vs solid) and the KPI card shows before/after total distance, avg distance per order and avg pick time per order on the opt set and the held-out set; "Baseline" button applies the fast-movers-nearest-dock assignment (pick lines desc -> dock distance asc) and scores it with the same `simulate`; the SA optimiser is an additional, clearly labelled opponent, not a substitute for the required baseline.
stretch_goals: Rack-visit and floor heatmap (InstancedMesh instanceColor accumulated from the simulator's per-order node paths; toggle between pick-frequency heat and visit heat) — nearly free, ~1 h
Leaderboard of player layouts (localStorage; name + held-out km + hash link) and share-by-URL (112-byte slot permutation base64 in the hash) so judges can open a layout on their phone — ~1.5 h
Batch picking: cart capacity C lines (default 24) / max 3 orders per trip, seed-and-savings batching, measured metres saved per order vs single-order picking on the held-out set — ~3 h

Two pickers with aisle congestion: time-stepped replay where a picker waits at an aisle entrance while another occupies that aisle (one-at-a-time aisle rule), reported as extra seconds per order vs no-congestion — ~3 h
Routing policy ablation UI (optimal DP vs S-shape vs return vs nearest-neighbour) with per-order path overlay — ~1 h since all policies exist in sim/route.ts
Configurable layout (aisles x bays, dock position centre vs corner, middle cross-aisle) with instant re-score, showing that conclusions hold across layouts — ~2 h
Offline-precomputed SA layout plus live 'watch it optimise' run with objective curve and temperature readout — ~1 h on top of the core SA
data_plan: Dataset: Online Retail II (UCI ML Repository id 502, Chen 2019, DOI 10.24432/C5CG6D), licence CC BY 4.0; 1,067,371 transaction rows Dec 2009–Dec 2011; columns Invoice, StockCode, Description, Quantity, InvoiceDate, Price, Customer ID, Country. Obtain tonight (22:00) with the VERIFIED mirror: `curl -L -o data/raw/online_retail_II.parquet "https://huggingface.co/datasets/vancevo/online-retail-ii/resolve/main/data/train-00000-of-00001.parquet"` (7.16 MB, PAR1 magic verified, both sheets merged). Fallbacks in `data/README.md`: Kaggle anonymous `https://www.kaggle.com/api/v1/datasets/download/mashlyn/online-retail-ii-uci` (15.2 MB zip -> 94.85 MB CSV) and the UCI zip `https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/502/online+retail+ii.zip` (43.5 MB, truncates from campus; last resort). Commit the 7 MB parquet under data/raw (well under 100 MB) so prep is reproducible offline. Preprocessing (`prep/prep.py`, Python 3.12, pandas 3.0.6 + pyarrow 26.0.0, run with `python -I`): month = Nov 2011 (peak); drop Invoice LIKE 'C%'; drop Quantity <= 0 and Price <= 0; drop null Description; drop exact duplicate rows (count reported); keep StockCode ~ `^\d{5}[A-Za-z]{0,2}$` (case-insensitive) and explicitly reject POST, D, M, S, DOT, BANK CHARGES, CRUK, ADJUST, AMAZONFEE, C2, PADS, TEST*, gift_*; pick lines = distinct (Invoice, StockCode) pairs; top-100 SKUs by pick lines; orders = invoices restricted to top-100 lines, keep all with >= 1 line (single-line orders still walk to the dock and back; count reported), lines per order deduplicated by SKU; time-based split: InvoiceDate < 2011-11-16 -> opt set, >= 2011-11-16 -> held-out set. Emit meta counts at every stage plus coverage_pct = lines_top100 / lines_after_nonproduct, generated_at and script sha. Expected scale (verify, do not quote until prep runs): ~80k raw lines in the month, ~2–3k orders after restriction, median 3–6 lines per order, coverage ~20–30%. Held-out evaluation: the SA optimiser and the player only see opt-set scores while editing; the KPI card and README headline the held-out set; the drift test ties README to `npm run eval`. The warehouse layout, walking speed (1.2 m/s), handling time (8 s/line), and the "original" layout convention (StockCode ascending, row-major from the far end) are declared design assumptions, labelled as such in README section "Data and assumptions" and in the in-app Data panel. Attribution text (README + Data panel): "Online Retail II, UCI Machine Learning Repository, Daqing Chen, CC BY 4.0; accessed via the Hugging Face mirror vancevo/online-retail-ii on 21 Oct 2026." No personal data is used (Customer ID is dropped at prep).
architecture: Everything runs in the browser; there is no backend, no API key, no env secret (`.env.example` contains only commented `VITE_PUBLIC_URL` with a note that the app has no secrets). Components: (1) `prep/prep.py` (offline, Python 3.12) -> `public/data/orders_2011-11.json` (< 1 MB) and `public/layouts/sa_seed42.json`. (2) `src/sim/` pure TypeScript, zero DOM: `layout.ts` (config -> nodes/edges, Dijkstra all-pairs Float32Array), `route.ts` (heldKarp, nnTwoOptOrOpt, sShape, returnPolicy), `simulate.ts` (orders -> totals + per-order node paths), `slotting.ts` (originalLayout, fastMoverBaseline, anneal with incremental delta), `types.ts` (shared interfaces, committed first). (3) `src/sim.worker.ts`: message protocol {simulate, anneal, cancel} -> {result, progress, annealDone}; keeps the main thread at 60 fps. (4) `src/store.ts` (zustand 5): layout permutation, selection, results per layout per set, replay state, quality tier, leaderboard. (5) `src/scene/` (R3F 9.8.2 + drei 10.7.9 + three 0.186.1): Racks (Instances), Boxes (InstancedMesh + instanceColor + fly lerp), FloorHeat (InstancedMesh), Picker/Ghost (procedural rig following node paths), RoutePath (drei Line), Dock, CameraRig (CameraControls presets), Effects (Bloom/SMAA gated by tier). (6) `src/ui/` (React 19 + Tailwind 4 + motion 14): HUD counters, KPI card, Data panel, Evidence panel, Slot map (SVG), controls, leaderboard, share link. (7) `eval/run.ts` (tsx) imports `src/sim` directly in Node to write `eval/results.md`; vitest tests in `src/sim/__tests__`. Data flow: JSON fetch -> store -> worker.simulate(layout, set) -> totals + per-order paths -> KPI card and replay animation; player edits -> store -> re-simulate (debounced 300 ms) -> both pickers' paths. Deployment: `vite build` -> static `dist/`; primary Vercel Hobby (static, `vercel.json` framework vite), mirror Cloudflare Pages (`wrangler pages deploy dist`), optional GitHub Pages via Actions; all three serve identical builds; demo laptop also runs `npm run preview` locally. No network calls after first load (no CDN fonts, no HDR environment, no map tiles, no analytics). Bundle: three + R3F + drei ~ 700 KB gzipped, JSON < 1 MB; load < 3 s on venue Wi-Fi, pre-loaded before the slot.
stack: @react-three/drei@10.7.9 (CameraControls via camera-controls@3.1.2, Instances, Line, DragControls, Html)
@react-three/postprocessing@3.2.1 + postprocessing@6.39.5 (Bloom, SMAA; peer three <0.187 satisfied; gated by quality tier, droppable if any issue)
motion@14.5.0 (counters, panel stagger, KPI layout animations)
Python 3.12 for prep: pandas==3.0.6, pyarrow==26.0.0 (duckdb==2.0.0 optional for the one-liner month filter)
Hosting: Vercel Hobby static (primary), Cloudflare Pages Free (mirror), optional GitHub Pages; local `vite preview` fallback
No LLM, no backend, no external runtime services
build_plan:
Interfaces first: Agent A commits `src/sim/types.ts` (LayoutConfig, Layout, Order, SimResult, PerOrderTrace, WorkerMessages) and a mock JSON within 30 min so B, C and D code against it. All agents work on branches feat/*, fast-forward to main at least hourly with conventional messages; Agent D enforces the cadence.

Agent A — Data + simulation core (~5 h, 22:00–03:00): prep.py with meta counts and tests (1 h, JSON committed by 23:00 = M1); layout graph + Dijkstra all-pairs (0.5 h); heldKarp + NN/2-opt/Or-opt + sShape/return with vitest vs brute force (1 h); simulate + fastMoverBaseline + originalLayout (0.5 h); Worker protocol (0.5 h); SA with SKU->orders index, incremental delta, subsample, time budget, progress stream, property test (1.5 h); then eval/run.ts + drift test + offline `sa_seed42.json` (overnight, 1 h).

Agent B — 3D scene (~6 h, 22:30–04:30): Canvas, lights, dark theme, Racks/Boxes/Floor instancing, dock (1 h); picker rig + path following from node paths + growing Line + box pulse (1.5 h); ghost picker + replay race choreography (1 h); box-fly relayout lerp (0.5 h); CameraControls presets + intro flight + follow cam (0.5 h); post-FX + quality tier probe + dpr cap + demand/always frameloop (1 h); perf pass on an Intel-iGPU laptop, draw-call audit < 50 (0.5 h).

Agent C — Game UI + state (~5 h, 22:30–03:30): zustand store + JSON loading + worker client with debounce (1 h); HUD counters, KPI card (Original/Baseline/SA/Player x opt/held-out), Data panel with meta verbatim, Evidence panel (1.5 h); 2D slot map with click-to-swap + affinity hints + drei DragControls snapping in 3D (1.5 h); replay controls, speed slider, routing policy toggle, leaderboard (localStorage), share-link hash encode/decode (1 h).

Agent D — Repo, deploy, docs, eval, deck (~4 h spread 21:45–13:30): repo scaffold, LICENSE MIT, .gitignore, .env.example, README skeleton with all required sections, DEV_LOG.md with the 18:00–21:30 planning note (first commit by 21:50); Vercel + Cloudflare Pages deploys of the walking skeleton by 02:30 (progress-review goodwill); hourly commit watchdog; README sections filled as modules land (architecture Mermaid, assumptions, data rules, must-have checklist with screenshots); eval/results.md regeneration at freeze; python-pptx 10-slide deck; demo script and Q&A cards; LinkedIn/X post drafts with #NEXAI2026.

Integration + QA (humans + one agent, ~4 h): 03:30–05:00 merge, end-to-end replay race on real data, fix; 07:30–09:30 humans read every module line-by-line with the agents' doc comments, assign file owners in README, run the full demo on a second laptop and phone (2D mode), Chrome/Edge/Firefox; 09:30–11:00 measured stretch goals only (heatmap, leaderboard/share, then batch picking or congestion if green); 11:00 feature freeze, tag; 11:00–12:30 `npm run eval`, README/DEV_LOG final, drift test green; 12:30–13:30 record 5-min demo + 3-min YouTube cut; 13:30–14:15 posts + YouTube; 14:15–14:45 smoke test all three URLs on a different laptop; 14:45 submit. Total agent effort ~24 h in parallel within ~15 wall-clock hours; humans sleep 01:30–07:30 while agents keep committing hourly.
risks: Laptop GPU stutter on the projector machine -> instancing keeps draw calls < 50, dpr capped at 1.5, no shadows/env maps, quality tier auto-probe disables Bloom/SMAA, frameloop demand when idle; tested on an Intel-iGPU laptop by 09:00; 2D slot-map mode is a complete fallback.

3D drag-and-drop is fiddly on stage -> click-to-swap in 3D and in the 2D slot map is the primary interaction; DragControls is an enhancement; rehearsed layout is one click away via the share-link hash.

Top-100 SKUs cover only ~20–30% of order lines -> state coverage % on screen and in README; slot count is configurable (8x2x10 = 160 slots for top-150 if time allows); never claim whole-warehouse savings.

SA shows little or no gain over the baseline, or runs too slowly -> SA starts from the baseline so it cannot be worse in-sample; incremental delta + 600-order subsample + time budget; shipped offline 60 s result; whatever the number is, it is reported honestly with the held-out gap.
Held-out gain much smaller than in-sample -> expected and narrated as the honesty story; both numbers always shown side by side.

HF parquet mirror unavailable tonight -> download now, commit the 7 MB parquet; Kaggle anonymous zip and UCI zip as documented fallbacks; prep output JSON is committed so the app never depends on raw data at runtime.

Commit-history gate (hourly, no bulk) -> Agent D watchdog; branches merged hourly with conventional messages; first commit by 21:50 with DEV_LOG planning note; tags mvp-m1/m2/m3, eval-frozen, feature-freeze, submission.
Humans must explain agent-written code -> small pure TS modules with doc comments and tests; 07:30–09:30 read-through; README owner table; 10 Q&A cards.
Vercel outage or venue Wi-Fi failure -> Cloudflare Pages mirror, optional GitHub Pages, local `vite preview` on two laptops, MP4 recording, phone hotspot.
postprocessing peer-dependency or WebGL quirk -> post-FX isolated behind the quality tier and a feature flag; drop it without touching the rest.
Orders with > 12 stops are routed heuristically, not exactly -> flagged per order and counted in the Evidence panel; same policy for before/after so comparisons stay fair.
Judges expect data-drive proof -> invoice IDs on the HUD, clickable boxes showing StockCode and pick counts from the JSON, meta counts verbatim, replay-twice determinism.
honesty_plan: Every number on screen is computed live by the same `simulate` function the eval script runs; `npm run eval` writes `eval/results.md` with commit hash and timestamp, and a vitest drift test fails CI if the committed results differ from a fresh run, so README, app and deck cannot disagree. Held-out split is time-based and shown in-app (opt = 1–15 Nov 2011, held-out = 16–30 Nov); the optimiser and the player only optimise on the opt set; headline metrics are held-out; the in-sample vs held-out gap for SA is printed, not hidden. Data provenance: UCI Online Retail II, CC BY 4.0, cited with DOI and the HF mirror; cleaning rules with row counts at each stage (C-invoices, non-product codes listed explicitly, negative/zero quantity or price, duplicates) in README "Data rules" and in the Data panel; coverage % of lines represented by the top-100 SKUs stated prominently. Declared assumptions, labelled as design choices and not data: warehouse geometry (8 aisles x 2 sides x 7 bays, 1.2 m pitch, 3 m aisles, corner dock), walking speed 1.2 m/s, 8 s handling per line, picker stands on the aisle centre line serving both sides, single-level racks, no cube/weight, the "original" layout convention (StockCode ascending). Limitations stated in README and spoken in the pitch: top-100 forward-pick area only; orders > 12 stops routed heuristically (count shown); no congestion unless the stretch is measured; 2011 UK gift-retailer data, not an Indian warehouse; results depend on the chosen layout (configurable layout stretch demonstrates sensitivity). Watch-outs honoured explicitly: cancelled invoices and non-product codes removed before counting picks (counts shown), walking follows the aisle graph (path overlay proves it), geometry kept simple for an average laptop (quality tier). No secrets exist; `.env.example` says so; no scraped or personal data (Customer ID dropped). AI tools declared in README: Claude Code agents wrote scaffolding, sim, scene and docs; humans reviewed every module, re-ran tests and eval, and own named files. Determinism: replaying twice gives identical metres; seeds for SA shown. Stretch goals are reported only with measured numbers from the same simulator; nothing is marked done without a metric.
